title: Transient amplification profile of a linear update
purpose: Compute ||A^h||_2 over a horizon for a linear update x_(h+1) = A x_h, with the peak, the step after which the norm stays below 1, the spectral radius and the Gelfand bound. Use it to find updates that are stable in the limit but amplify perturbations first.

entry_points.name: transient_profile
entry_points.arguments: matrix: square A (at most 60 rows); horizon: integer 1 to 5000
entry_points.returns: {norms for h = 0..horizon, peak_norm, peak_step, amplifies, settles_below_one_at, spectral_radius (null above size 8), gelfand_bound, converged}

entry_points.name: spectral_norm
entry_points.arguments: matrix: any rectangular matrix; iterations; tolerance

assumptions: The update is linear and time-invariant: the same A at every step.
Norms are Euclidean (spectral) norms; another norm gives another profile.
guarantees: Each norm is the Rayleigh-quotient limit of power iteration on B^T B from two deterministic starts; the tests match closed forms to 1e-12.
gelfand_bound = min over h >= 1 of ||A^h||^(1/h) is an upper bound on the spectral radius.
settles_below_one_at is the first step from which every norm up to the horizon is below 1, or null.

known_wrong.name: radius_below_one_still_amplifies
known_wrong.why: Reading stability from eigenvalues alone predicts monotone decay 0.8^h; the non-normal coupling amplifies about eightfold first.

known_wrong.name: fourth_power_is_not_eigenvalue_forecast
known_wrong.why: 0.8^4 is the eigenvalue-only forecast of ||A^4||; the true norm is about 8.21.

limits: Dense powers by repeated multiplication: meant for matrices up to about 60 rows and horizons up to a few thousand steps. Power iteration converges slowly when the top two singular values nearly coincide; the result reports converged. Eigenvalues come from the characteristic polynomial, so they are limited to 8 rows and a repeated eigenvalue is accurate to about 1e-8. Linear time-invariant updates only; it does not model nonlinear or time-varying dynamics.
technique_references: Pseudospectra and non-normal transient growth (Trefethen and Embree)
